newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Wide price differences in EU car insurance.
newsitem.headline: Wide price differences in EU car insurance.

text.p: A young driver living in Berlin pays about four times more for basic car insurance than somebody of the same age in Lisbon, according to a survey comparing European car insurance premiums published on Thursday.

The study by the European Consumers' Organisation (BEUC) and the Association des Consommateurs Test Achats, a Belgian consumer organisation, compared prices for motor vehicle insurance in eight European Union countries.

"Consumers across Europe pay vastly different prices for their car insurance," they said in a statement. Because of this, "it would be interesting for EU citizens to be able to take out motor vehicle insurance with a foreign company."
But the absence of a real internal insurance market in the 15-nation EU hampered competition and prevented consumers from shopping around freely for the best deal.
Taxes and differences in insurance coverage also helped explain the huge price gaps.

BEUC and Test Achats asked insurers in Portugal, Spain, Netherlands, Belgium, Italy, Britain, France and Germany about premiums on five different cars, both for young, first-time drivers and for older, more experienced drivers.
They asked for quotes for these drivers both if they lived in the capital or in a small village.

For a young person living in the capital and driving a VW Golf, the yearly average premium for basic third party car insurance ranged from only 346 European currency units ($390) in Portugal to as much as 1,391 Ecus in Germany.
"However, prices within countries can also vary significantly. It is therefore worthwhile for consumers to shop around before buying insurance," the statement said.
It mentioned the case of British company Direct Line which turns away young people driving BMWs or Mercedes but "for those whom it does accept, it offers interesting prices."
For experienced drivers with a clean record, both Spain and the Netherlands are interesting, it said. However, "Belgian companies are very expensive even for good drivers."
In theory, drivers can take out motor vehicle insurance in another EU country as the single insurance market was introduced on July 1, 1994.
But even if there are certain minimum rules for insurers wishing to attract clients in another EU country, the single market is not yet a reality, BEUC and Test Achats said.

Significant differences in contractual terms between insurance policies in different member states make comparisons difficult for consumers. "There is also widely varying treatment for different categories of drivers."
Existing EU rules limit consumers who want to shop around.

"For these and other reasons, if a French consumer wants to buy an insurance policy in Spain, where the price is more interesting, it is unlikely that he would find a Spanish company willing to offer him a cheap insurance policy."

BEUC and Test Achats called on the European Commission to create a single market for consumers, including harmonisation of laws governing insurance contracts and steps to allow and encourage consumers to shop around between member states. ($1=0.88 Ecu)
